statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band as long-end yields retreat from multi-decade highs and the overnight price path stays orderly.
recommendation: Tail holds below the watch threshold on an orderly path with a genuine overnight retracement already printed. The 13:30Z U.S. cash open is the narrow evidence-based checkpoint, where a record-high entry with cooperative yields and oil could begin to deny retracement.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures extend to a new session high while the ten-year yield backs off its 2002 peak and Brent slips under $100; Tail stays low, Stress eases slightly to elevated.
body: NQ December futures trade at 31,493.25, up 175.50 or 0.56%, roughly 15 points below the 31,508.00 session high inside a 199-point range whose 31,309.25 low confirms a genuine retracement has already occurred in this window. Cash NASDAQ-100 closed Monday at 31,076.44, up 0.87%, a record, with Monday's 31,117.36 high also the 52-week high. VIX is 15.34, down 1.16%, sitting at the low of its 15.34-15.52 range. The decisive change since the previous assessment is in cross-asset conditions, which have moved from amplifying to relieving. The ten-year Treasury yield is 5.266%, down 4.7bp from a 5.313% close and off a 5.329% session high that marked the highest level since 2002; the thirty-year has retreated to about 5.63% from a 5.702% peak, and the two-year is essentially unchanged near the 4.83% of the latest H.15 release. Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly committed to bending the debt trajectory, though analysts note that without concrete deficit plans the statement alone is unlikely to reverse the selloff. Brent at $98.22 and WTI at $87.49, both down about 2%, extend a multi-session decline as Middle East exports recover and the G7 agreed to release 100 million barrels from emergency reserves; Brent is back below $100. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed pending Iran's stated conditions, with an Iran-Oman corridor near final but short of normal transit. That is a persistent condition rather than new escalation. Equity futures are broadly higher with the Dow leading, European equities extended a third session of gains and semiconductor leadership is firm in pre-market trade, though internals stay narrow and mixed. Against the single genuine Tail amplifier of an index holding within fifteen points of its session high in a record regime stand a decaying VIX, an already-printed overnight pullback, and macro drivers that are now easing rather than tightening. Tail is therefore held at 15 with a conditional lift confined to the opening auction.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail opened the window at 9 on Monday morning, dipped to 7 by 12:00Z, then climbed through the U.S. session to a 20 peak at 19:00Z as the index pushed to a record close, the only watch-band reading of the window. It decayed steadily overnight into an 8-12 band and then firmed again to 12 at 09:00Z and 13 at 10:00Z as European trade lifted futures toward a new session high. Stress held in a 45-55 elevated band throughout and Confidence stayed in a tight 86-89 range. Mode alternated between mixed and trend-up, with a single normal reading at 12:00Z.
outlookSummary: The orderly path is expected to persist through the remainder of the European morning with Tail held at 15. Risk stays concentrated in the narrow 13:30Z-15:00Z U.S. opening window, where the index would enter the auction at record highs with yields and oil both cooperating; conditional Tail is lifted to 18-19 there, the peak of the window, and again to 18 into the 19:00Z power hour and 17 through the 20:00Z cash close. Conditional Tail then decays to a 10-12 floor across the Asian session before a measured climb back to 14 with the European open a day on. Every forecast hour stays below the watch threshold, so the mapped policy state remains EA_ON across the window. Stress eases to a 44-51 band, lower than the previous assessment because the long end has retreated from its 2002 high and Brent has slipped under $100, but still elevated because a 5.27% ten-year, a closed Strait of Hormuz and narrow index leadership are unchanged. Confidence tapers from 88 to 77 with horizon decay. Scheduled catalysts beyond the window, notably the September FOMC minutes at 2026-10-07T18:00Z and the 10-Year Note auction an hour earlier, are carried in the event calendar rather than the forecast.
